metadata.title: The Watch That Did Not Come Back

series.title: The Quiet Seals
series.episodeTitle: The Watch That Did Not Come Back

setup.pitch: Hearthford’s night watch marched into the fog. At dawn, their footprints came back without them.
setup.gmSummary: Six watchfolk followed a horn beyond Eastbarrow and vanished. Their footprints returned to the gate by themselves. An old muster-stone is another Quiet Seal: it once bound a dead company to defend the road, but Captain Vale broke the stone trying to call help during a raid. The dead now mistake every armed traveler for a deserter. Clock: at midnight the dead company marches through Hearthford to collect six replacements. The party can repair the muster, release the company, bargain for a new oath, or break the seal and fight its captain. Three required facts have redundant physical and NPC sources; no named NPC is required.
setup.campaignFrame: A self-contained Quiet Seals night. Prior endings may color Oda’s dialogue but do not change the adventure graph.

quest.objective: Find the missing watch and stop the dead company before midnight.
quest.stakes: At midnight the dead company enters Hearthford and takes six living replacements.
quest.deadline: Midnight; show a four-step clock: sunset, first horn, second horn, midnight.
successConditions: The six watchfolk are freed or their fate is knowingly resolved.
The dead company cannot claim six Hearthford replacements at midnight.
failureConditions: Midnight arrives with the oath unresolved and Hearthford undefended.

facts.text: The Eastbarrow muster-stone is a Quiet Seal binding a dead road-company to an old defensive oath.
Captain Elian Vale cracked the muster-stone while desperately trying to summon the old defenders during a raid.
At midnight the dead company will enter Hearthford and claim six living replacements unless its oath is resolved.

secrets.text: The dead captain is obeying the exact last order carved beneath the broken stone: HOLD SIX UNTIL RELIEVED.
secrets.revealCondition: Read the lower inscription, hear Watcher Nessa repeat the dead captain’s words, or question the dead standard-bearer.

npcs.name: Reeve Oda Flint
voiceCues: Counts missing people on her fingers.
cannotKnow: What Vale did at the stone
npcs.questFunction: Points the party east; if unavailable, the returned footprints and gate log do the same job.

npcs.name: Watcher Nessa Reed
voiceCues: Whispers so the dead do not count her.
knows: The dead demand six people until relieved
believes: The company can be reasoned with
cannotKnow: Which final solution the party will choose
npcs.questFunction: Human face of the rescue and one clue source.

npcs.name: Captain Elian Vale
voiceCues: Answers tactical questions immediately and moral questions slowly.
fears: Being remembered as the man who doomed the watch
knows: He cracked the stone with a hammer during the raid
believes: Repairing the stone may restore the old oath
lies: Initially says the stone was already cracked
npcs.questFunction: Optional confession and repair aid; not required.

locations.name: Hearthford East Gate
locations.description: Mud, gatehouse, and six sets of bootprints that end facing inward with no owners.

locations.name: Eastbarrow Road
locations.description: A hedged military road where fog lies ankle-deep and old mileposts bear scratched tally marks.

locations.name: Abandoned Watch Camp
locations.description: Cold cookfire, six bedrolls, and a torn duty roster pinned under a cup.

locations.name: Broken Muster Field
locations.description: A 70-by-60-foot field around a split standing stone; six living watchfolk kneel inside a ring of spectral spearpoints.

scenes.title: 1. The Footprints Came Home
scenes.purpose: Hook the party, put the midnight clock on the table, and point east without requiring Oda.
scenes.readAloud: Six lines of muddy bootprints cross the east bridge and stop beneath Hearthford’s gate. No boots stand in them. Beyond the wall, a horn sounds once from the dark hills. Oda Flint holds up the watch ledger. ‘Six went out. Their tracks came back. They did not.’
gmNotes: Objective: follow the returned tracks east before the second horn.

DC 12 Wisdom (Survival): the tracks are the watch’s exact boot patterns, but the impressions point toward town as if made by invisible walkers. Failure: a broken watch badge beside the road still points east.
Physical clue: gate ledger says the patrol went to inspect Eastbarrow’s old muster-stone.
Clock starts at sunset. Advance to first horn after the road scene, second horn on entering the muster field, midnight after roughly 4 hours or a deliberate long delay.

scenes.title: 2. The Toll of the Old Road
scenes.purpose: Give fight/sneak/talk options and establish that the dead enforce an oath rather than hunt randomly.
scenes.readAloud: Fog fills the ditches like pale water. Three armored figures stand across the road beneath a rotted banner. Their shields bear no crest, only six vertical cuts. The center figure lowers a spear. ‘Name your watch. Name who relieves you.’
gmNotes: Objective: pass the old sentries without spending too much time or blood.

Talk-out: DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) while claiming to be relief. Success: they salute and allow passage; the party learns the phrase HOLD SIX UNTIL RELIEVED. Failure: they demand one weapon as surety; refusal starts combat.
Sneak: DC 13 group Dexterity (Stealth) through the hedge. Failure starts combat with the party 30 feet from the sentries.

Combat: 3 Oathbound Sentries, AC 13, HP 16 each, speed 30 ft.; Spear +4, 1d6+2 piercing; formation reaction once/round: when an adjacent sentry is hit, add +2 AC to the target, potentially causing the attack to miss. They stop fighting if shown the duty roster or given a credible relief order.
Map: road 15 ft. wide; hedges provide half cover; ditch is difficult terrain; sentries start 30 ft. ahead.

scenes.title: 3. Six Names on the Roster
scenes.purpose: Deliver the puzzle, Vale’s guilt, and a physical fail-safe clue before the finale.
scenes.readAloud: The watch camp is laid for six people who never slept here. Six bedrolls. Six tin cups. Six names on a duty roster. A seventh line has been scratched so hard the parchment tore: RELIEF — NONE.
gmNotes: Puzzle: six brass duty tags hang on pegs marked DAWN, NOON, DUSK, MIDNIGHT, RELIEF, and RETURN. The roster records the old watch cycle: Dawn → Noon → Dusk → Midnight → Relief → Return. Put the six tags in that order to open the dispatch box.

Solution is printed above. DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation or History) bypass spots wear marks showing the order. Fail-forward: after two wrong attempts the box opens but the first horn sounds and the party loses the prepared advantage in the finale.
Inside: Vale’s unsent confession, a charcoal rubbing of the stone’s lower words HOLD SIX UNTIL RELIEVED, and mason’s wire useful for repair.

Trap: lifting the roster without first pinning the black wax seal triggers a memory-horn. DC 13 Wisdom save; failure 2d6 psychic damage and deafened until the end of the character’s next turn; success half damage. Either way the dispatch box remains accessible.
Optional DC 12 Wisdom (Insight) when confronting Vale later: he is ashamed, not malicious.

scenes.title: 4. Hold Six Until Relieved
scenes.purpose: Rescue the watch through repair, release, bargain, or battle while the objective changes the encounter.
scenes.readAloud: The standing stone has split from crown to base. Six living watchfolk kneel around it, awake and rigid. Beyond them waits a line of dead soldiers, transparent beneath old mail. Their captain plants a broken standard in the earth. ‘Six held,’ he says. ‘Name the relief.’
gmNotes: Objective: resolve the oath before midnight; killing the captain is only one option.
Nessa can speak if a character reaches her. She confirms the dead repeat HOLD SIX UNTIL RELIEVED.

REPAIR: 3 successes before 2 failures, one action each, DC 13 Strength (Athletics) to brace, Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) to wire, or Intelligence (Arcana/Religion) to restore the carved oath. Camp wire grants the first success automatically. Success restores the old defensive oath and frees the six.

RELEASE: expose the complete lower inscription, then DC 14 Charisma (Persuasion) to convince the captain that Hearthford itself is lawful relief. If the party has the roster/rubbing, make this DC 12. Success lets the company stand down forever.

BARGAIN: offer a new watch oath. DC 14 Charisma (Persuasion); on success one willing character promises to return at next new moon to formally dismiss the company. The six go free now; breaking the promise is a campaign consequence, not a trap sprung tonight.

BREAK: destroy the stone (AC 15, 30 HP, immune psychic/poison). Doing so frees the six but makes the dead captain corporeal and hostile. Captain of the Last Watch: AC 15, HP 58, speed 30; Longsword +5, 1d8+3 slashing plus 1d4 necrotic; Multiattack two longswords; Command the Line (recharge 5–6): each sentry may move up to half speed without opportunity attacks. Two Oathbound Sentries fight beside him. Captain yields at 10 HP if shown the roster and offered lawful relief.
Prepared advantage: if the dispatch box was solved before two failures, the party may place the roster at the stone; the captain cannot use Command the Line in round 1.
Map: 70x60 ft.; stone center; six captives in a 15-ft. ring; captain 20 ft. north; two sentries 15 ft. east/west; low wall south gives half cover.

scenes.title: 5. The Empty Seventh Place
scenes.purpose: Pay the party, reveal the wider pattern, and record the chosen consequence.
scenes.readAloud: At Hearthford’s gate, six watch cloaks hang from six shoulders again. Oda counts them twice before she looks at you. Far behind, Eastbarrow’s horn gives one last note — or, if you broke the stone, none at all. On the old duty ledger, a seventh line has appeared in faded ink: HEARTHFORD — RELIEVED.
gmNotes: Reward: 200 gp total from Hearthford plus the recovered silver watch-badge worth 50 gp if the party returns all six alive.
If repaired: the road gains spectral defenders; travelers report safer nights.
If released: the muster field becomes quiet and ordinary.
If bargained: record who owes the new-moon promise.
If broken: Hearthford is safe tonight, but the old road loses its supernatural defense.
Campaign revelation: another Quiet Seal was built as a bargain with a protective purpose, not merely a prison.

clues.revelation: The muster-stone is a Quiet Seal binding an old defensive company.
sources: Physical: gate ledger names the old muster-stone and bears the same seal-mark seen on prior Quiet Seals.
NPC: Vale explains the old local story of defenders called from the stone.
Physical: the dispatch-box rubbing shows the binding circle and oath around the stone.

clues.revelation: Vale cracked the stone while trying to summon help during a raid.
sources: Physical: Vale’s unsent confession in the camp dispatch box.
NPC: Vale confesses when shown the rubbing or challenged with tool marks.
Physical: fresh hammer scars on the crack match Vale’s watch hammer at the camp.

clues.revelation: The company must hold six until relieved and will take six replacements at midnight.
sources: Physical: lower inscription reads HOLD SIX UNTIL RELIEVED; a second line marks MIDNIGHT MUSTER.
NPC: Nessa heard the dead captain announce the midnight replacement.
NPC/encounter: road sentries repeat the relief demand and six-count.

encounters.objective: Pass the sentries by talk, stealth, or combat.
encounters.bypass: Credible relief order or successful group Stealth.

creatures.name: Oathbound Sentry
creatures.trait: Formation Guard (reaction, once per round per group): +2 AC to an adjacent sentry against one triggering attack.
creatures.morale: Stops if lawfully relieved; never pursues toward Hearthford.

encounters.difficulty: Moderate-to-High only if the party chooses violence
encounters.objective: Free the six and resolve the oath.
encounters.bypass: Repair, release, or bargain ends the encounter without killing the dead.

creatures.name: Captain of the Last Watch
creatures.attack: Longsword +5 to hit, 1d8+3 slashing plus 1d4 necrotic; two attacks on his turn.
creatures.action: Command the Line (Recharge 5–6): each allied Oathbound Sentry moves up to half speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
creatures.morale: Yields at 10 HP if offered lawful relief.

puzzles.solution: Dawn → Noon → Dusk → Midnight → Relief → Return
puzzles.bypass: DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation or History) reveals peg wear and solves it.
puzzles.failForward: After two wrong attempts the box opens anyway, but the first horn sounds and the finale prepared advantage is lost.

traps.trigger: Lift the duty roster without pinning the black wax seal.
traps.failure: 2d6 psychic damage and deafened until end of the character’s next turn.
traps.failForward: The dispatch box and all required clues remain accessible.

items.name: Old Duty Roster
items.use: Proof of the old watch cycle and lawful relief; lowers RELEASE DC to 12.

items.name: Mason’s Binding Wire
items.use: Grants the first REPAIR success automatically.

policies: No named NPC is required to reach or resolve the finale.
Failed checks change cost or position; they do not erase required facts.
If a core scene is bypassed, use an authored physical clue at the muster field rather than inventing a new fact.

routes.trigger: Oda is refused, absent, or dead.
routes.response: The gate ledger, returned footprints, and a watch badge point directly to Eastbarrow.
At the muster field the lower inscription is exposed enough to read; Nessa can state the midnight threat. Repair has no automatic wire success.

routes.trigger: Vale is attacked, absent, or never questioned.
routes.response: His physical confession and matching hammer scars establish how the stone broke.

cutOrder: Shorten road combat after two sentries fall; the last yields.
Skip extended Vale confrontation and use his written confession.

endings.title: The Watch Restored
endings.result: The six live and the old company resumes defending the road.

endings.title: Honorably Relieved
endings.condition: Prove lawful relief and persuade the captain.
endings.result: The six live and the dead company finally rests.

endings.title: A New Watch
endings.condition: Make a new oath with the captain.
endings.result: The six live; one or more heroes owe a new-moon return.

endings.title: No More Seal
endings.condition: Destroy the stone and survive or settle the resulting fight.
endings.result: The six live, but the old road loses its supernatural defense.

endings.title: Six Replacements
endings.condition: Reach midnight without resolving the oath.
endings.result: The dead march on Hearthford; the party can still confront them at the gate, but six townsfolk are marked as replacements until the oath is resolved.
